findings.text: assert child.rearmed_for == WORKING_RUN compares the census field against the run id this case itself handed to the stub live view, so the two sides move together: it pins only that the host echoes the view's return value, not that the name is the run that caused the re-arm. The same shape recurs at lines 171 and 234. The substantive spawn-count assertions beside them are independent and do carry the guard.

No case drives a delivered run whose review is unreconciled, which the plan's deliverable names as a re-arm trigger; that branch is inherited from station_subscriber.population_has_live_work and is left untested by this file, so a change to that rule would not redden this node's gate.

The non-settled exit branch does not clear child.rearmed_for (it is cleared only on settle, line 601), so a child that is re-armed and then crashes carries the earlier run id into the census written after its backoff restart, attributing that restart to a run that did not cause it.

The file is committed outside the run's declared write paths (reckon/crew/session_host.py, the landing fragment, the figures directory) even though the done-when names it as a write path; the fence list omitted it, so the record is inside its measure and outside its fence, and the coordinator has to add the path rather than the node drop the test.
